sentences.text: COMMON
ORAL ORDER 1.

By way of the present petition under Section 439(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ('the Code', in short), the petitioner State has prayed to quash and set aside the order passed by the concerned trial Court, granting bail to the accused persons in connection with the FIR bearing No.
I-40 of 2019, registered with Ramol Police Station, Ahmedabad City, under Sections 376(2)(n),
376D, 328 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Heard learned APP for the petitioner State and learned Advocate, Mr. Nanavati, and learned Advocate, Mr. Brahmbhatt, for the respective respondents-accused persons.

sentences.text: It is also required to be borne in mind that when a prayer is made for the cancellation of grant of bail cogent and overwhelming circumstances must be present and bail once granted cannot be cancelled in a mechanical manner without considering whether any supervening circumstances have rendered it in conducing to allow fair trial.

This proposition draws support from the Judgment of this Court in Daulat Ram and others v. State of Haryana reported in (1995) 1 SCC 349, Kashmira Singh v. Duman Singh (1996) 4 SCC 693 and xxx v. State of Telangana (2018) 16 SCC 511.'
4.

sentences.text: Learned APP appearing for the Respondent-State submitted that the victim as well as the fetus have passed away, even before the victim could enter the witness box.
However, it was submitted that the DNA sample was collected from the fetus, which matches with the DNA sample of Respondent No.2-original accused in Criminal Misc. Application No. 12462 of 2022.
Thereby, it was submitted that the concerned trial Court did not take into consideration the gravity of the offence.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/12451/2022 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 undefined
4.1 Learned APP also argued that the learned Sessions Court has failed to notice that the accused are charged with the offence under Sections 376(d) of the IPC.
Thereby, it was prayed that these applications be allowed.

5. On the other hand, learned Advocates appearing for the Respondents-accused strongly opposed these applications and prayed that the same be dismissed, as there is neither breach of any condition nor is there any supervening circumstances, which may warrant interference by this Court.
6. Having heard the learned Advocates for the parties and having perused the material on record, at the outset, it may be noted that the victim and the fetus, both have passed away.
Further, the report of the concerned trial Court indicates that the trial is going on smoothly and out of the total 67 witnesses, 19 witnesses, have already been examined.
There is no report to the effect that the Respondents-accused have misused their liberty during post-bail period.

Under the circumstances,
no case is made out to cancel the bail.

The cancellation of bail should not be done mechanically,
since, the same deals with the right of personal liberty of an accused, as enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

6.1 Further, report of the concerned Court indicates that the learned Judge, before whom the trial of the case was pending, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/12451/2022 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 undefined since, is posted as Principal District Judge, Navsari, now, the case is pending with the State Of Gujarat vs Chirag Amrutbhai Vaghela on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125435769/

Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, it is expected that the learned Principal District Judge shall explore the possibilities of putting the case before another Court so that the trial can progress further, expeditiously.

6.2 Learned APP, though, strongly argued to cancel the anticipatory bail on submission that the learned Sessions Court while granting bail did not consider the factors to be considered for granting or rejecting the bail, and failed to submit any supervening circumstances being rendered in conducing to allow fair trial.
Thus, this Court finds no circumstances to adjudge the impugned order as unjust and contrary to the settled principles of law.
As held earlier, the petitioner has failed to point out supervening circumstances, which may interfere with the fair trial.

7. Before parting with the order, I may also refer the observations made in the recent decision by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Kekhriesatuo Tep and others Vs.National Investigating Agency reported in (2023) 6 SCC 58.

sentences.text:
The relevant observation made in para 19 reads as under:-
"19. The learned Special Judge has himself distinguished cases of the persons who have indulged into extortion for furthering the activities of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/12451/2022 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 undefined organization and the persons like the present appellants, who were government servants, and compelled to contribute the amount.

We, therefore, find that it cannot be said that the prima facie opinion, as expressed by the learned Special Judge, could be said to be perverse or impossible."
8. Resultantly, present applications fail and are stand dismissed.
Interim relief, if any, stands vacated.
Rule / Notice is discharged.
